info.title: Foyer API
info.description: Curated indie game showcase: accounts, developer profiles, game pages, builds, the review queue and moderation. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with a session token from login or an API token. Player endpoints also accept tester keys in `X-Foyer-Key` (comma separated), which unlock unpublished games and private channels.

put.summary: Change a user's role. Admins only.

get.summary: Start a Discord sign-in: where to send the browser.

post.summary: Finish a Discord sign-in and start a session.

400.description: `discord_failed`, or `discord_email_unverified` when the Discord account has no verified email

409.description: `discord_email_taken`: the email's account is linked to another Discord account

post.summary: Log in with email or username and password.
Revoke the token used for this request.

Set a new password with the token from the reset link. Every session is
signed out; API tokens keep working. Also confirms the email address,
since the link proves the user can read it.

Email a password reset link. Answers 204 whether or not the address has
an account, so it can't be used to find out who is registered.

Create an account and start a session. A link to confirm the email
address is sent; until then the account can't submit games.

get.summary: List the caller's API tokens.

post.summary: Create an API token for the CLI or CI. The secret is returned only once.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's API tokens.

post.summary: Confirm an email address with the token from the link.
Send the confirmation link again.

get.summary: One build.

post.summary: Presigned download URLs for a ready build's chunks.

Check every chunk is uploaded and hand the build to the worker, which
scans it, packs its zip, marks it `ready` and points its channel at it.
Calling it again on a `processing` or `ready` build returns the build
unchanged.

get.summary: A build's manifest, for clients planning an install or update.

post.summary: Fresh upload URLs for the chunks a build is still missing.
Create the caller's developer profile. Each account can have one.

get.summary: A developer's public profile.
A developer's published games, newest first.

A developer's strikes, newest first, revoked ones included. The
developer and reviewers only.
Published games, newest first, or best match first when searching.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text search over title, tagline, tags, developer and
description. Every word must match; the last word may be a prefix.

post.summary: Create a game page as a draft. Needs a developer profile.

get.summary:
A game page. Unpublished games are visible only to their developer,
reviewers and tester keys for the game.
A game's appeals, newest first. Developer and reviewers only.

post.summary:
Appeal the game's latest decision, if it was a rejection or a delisting.
Each decision can be appealed once.

get.summary: Builds of a game, newest first. Developer and reviewers only.

post.summary: Start a build: send the manifest, get upload URLs for missing chunks.

get.summary:
A game's channels and the build each one serves. Players see only
channels with a ready build, and private channels only with a tester key
that covers them.

patch.summary:
Make a channel private or public. Players lose a private channel at
once; tester keys that cover it keep working.

post.summary:
A short-lived link to the zip of a channel's current build. Counts one
browser download.

404.description: No such game or channel, or no zip yet

get.summary:
Zips of each channel's current build, for the download buttons on the
game page. Builds whose zip is still being packed are left out.

post.summary:
Add an image to a game page and get a presigned URL to upload it to. A new
capsule replaces the old one.

delete.summary: Remove an image from a game page.

post.summary:
Report a published game to staff. Signing in is optional. A second
report from the same player while the first is still open is accepted
and ignored.

get.summary: Download counts of a game. Developer and reviewers only.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Days of daily counts, ending today. 1 to 365, default 30.

get.summary:
A game's submissions and their decisions, newest first. Developer and
reviewers only.

post.summary:
Submit a draft (or a game with requested changes) for review. Needs a
description and at least one ready build.

get.summary: A game's tester keys, newest first. Developer only.

post.summary:
Create a tester key. It unlocks the game before it is published, and
the listed channels (all when empty), private or not. The key is
returned only once, with a website link that unlocks the game.

delete.summary:
Revoke a tester key. Clients holding it lose access at once; games they
already installed keep working but get no more updates.

get.summary: The signed-in user.
The caller's developer profile.
The caller's games in every status, for the developer dashboard.
Appeals, oldest first. Reviewers only.

post.summary:
Decide an appeal. The reviewer who made the original decision can't,
unless they are an admin. Overturning publishes the game; reopening lets
the developer change it and resubmit. Both revoke the decision's strikes.
The developer gets an email either way.

Record a strike against a developer, optionally for one of their games.
Reviewers only.

Take a published game down for a policy violation. The reason is recorded
as a `delisting` in the game's history, the game's open reports are closed
as actioned, and the developer gets an email saying how to appeal.

get.summary: A game's reports, newest first (at most 200). Reviewers only.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only reports with this status. Default: all.

post.summary:
Close a game's open reports without acting on them. To act, delist the
game instead, which closes them as actioned. Reviewers only.

get.summary: Open submissions, oldest first. Reviewers only.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: Only submissions claimed by the caller.

get.summary:
Games with open reports. Games reported for malware come first, then
the most reported, then the longest waiting. Reviewers only.

post.summary: Take a strike back. Reviewers only.

Claim a submission, so other reviewers know it is taken. Admins can take
over another reviewer's claim.

Record a decision. Claims the submission if nobody has; admins can decide
on another reviewer's claim.

Put a claimed submission back in the queue. The claiming reviewer or an
admin can do this, so an abandoned claim never blocks a game.

Which game a tester key unlocks. Needs no account. Afterwards send the
key in `X-Foyer-Key` with every request for that game.

Which installed builds have updates. For the desktop client; send every
installed game in one call.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code, e.g. `not_found`, `validation`,
`missing_chunks`. Match on this, not on `message`.

missing.description: For `missing_chunks`: the chunk hashes that are not in storage yet.

ApiToken.description: An API token, without its secret.

Appeal.description:
A developer asking staff to look again at a rejection or a delisting.
Each decision can be appealed once.

decision_notes.description: The reviewer's answer. Visible to the developer.

ArchiveDownload.description:
`POST /v1/games/{slug}/channels/{channel}/archive`: a short-lived link
to the zip. Each call counts as one browser download.

AuthResponse.description: A new session. Send `token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

AvailableUpdate.description: A newer build for an installed game.

latest.description:
The channel's current build. Fetch its manifest and plan the patch
with `foyer_patch::diff`.

Build.description: One uploaded build of a game on a channel.

chunk_count.description: Number of distinct chunks in the manifest.

oneOf.description: What the desktop client should run, when the developer set it.
Result of the malware scan, once the worker has run it.

total_size.description: Sum of all file sizes in bytes.

version.description: Free-form version label set by the developer.

BuildScan.description: The malware scan of one build.

ChannelStatus.description: A channel and the build it currently serves.

private.description: Only tester keys, the developer and reviewers see private channels.

hash.description: Lowercase hex BLAKE3 hash of the chunk bytes.

ChunkUpload.description: Upload a chunk with `PUT url` and the chunk's bytes as the body.

ContentDescriptor.description: Content a player may want to know about before playing.

CreateApiTokenRequest.description: `POST /v1/auth/tokens`: a long-lived API token for the CLI or CI.

name.description: Shown in the token list, e.g. "GitHub Actions".

channel.description:
1 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`. A channel is
tied to the platform of its first build.

oneOf.description:
What the desktop client should run. `executable` must be a file in
the manifest.

private.description:
Make the channel private (`true`) or public (`false`). Left out, a
new channel is public and an existing one keeps its setting. Private
channels are only served to tester keys that cover them.

expires_at.description:
When the upload URLs stop working. Get fresh ones from
`POST /v1/builds/{id}/uploads`.

uploads.description:
Only the chunks storage does not have yet. Empty when every chunk was
uploaded before; call finalize right away.

slug.description: 2 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`.

CreateGame.description:
`POST /v1/games`. The game is created as a draft owned by the caller's
developer profile.

slug.description: 2 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`. Unique.

CreateMedia.description: `POST /v1/games/{slug}/media`: reserve an image and get an upload URL.

details.description: What the player saw. Required for `other`.

game.description: The slug of the developer's game it is for.

channels.description:
Channels to unlock; empty for all of them. Channels that don't exist
yet are fine, so a key can be handed out before the first push.

expires_in_days.description: Days until the key expires, 1 to 365. Default 30.

CreatedApiToken.description: Returned once, when a token is created. The secret cannot be read again.

link.description: A website link that unlocks the game in the visitor's browser.

secret.description: The key itself (`fyk_...`). Store it now; it can't be shown again.

strike.description: Record a strike against the developer. Only with `rejected`.
Record a strike against the developer too.

Developer.description: A developer (person or studio). Each user can own one.

DeveloperSummary.description: The developer as shown on a game.

state.description:
Also in `url`. Keep it (e.g. in a cookie) and check that the callback
carries the same value, so the sign-in can't be started by another
site.

DiscordCallback.description:
`POST /v1/auth/discord/callback`: the query parameters Discord sent the
browser back with.

notes.description: Why nothing needs doing. Staff only; reporters aren't told.

DownloadCounts.description: Downloads of one platform, or of one day.

DownloadEvent.description: Why the desktop client is downloading chunks.

oneOf.description:
Set on the first request of an install or update, so it is counted
once. Counts are anonymous.

hashes.description:
Chunks to download. Empty means every chunk in the build. At most
10 000 per request.

ai_disclosure.description:
How generative AI was used, if at all. Disclosure is required by the
content guidelines.

platforms.description: Platforms with at least one ready build.

GameDownload.description:
A zip of a channel's current build, for downloading in the browser
(`GET /v1/games/{slug}/downloads`).

archive_size.description: Size of the zip in bytes.

default.description:
True for the channel the game page offers for this platform: the one
named after the platform (`windows`), else the most recently updated.

daily.description:
One entry per day of the requested range, oldest first, including
days without downloads.

GameStatus.description: Where a game is in its life cycle. Only `published` games are public.

InstalledBuild.description: A build the desktop client has installed.

LaunchTarget.description: The file the desktop client starts, with its arguments.

executable.description: Manifest path of the executable, e.g. `bin/game.x86_64`.

chunks.description: The file's content-defined chunks, in order. Empty for an empty file.

executable.description: Unix `+x` after install. Omitted when false.

hash.description: Lowercase hex BLAKE3 hash of the file contents.

ManifestSchema.description: OpenAPI description of [`Manifest`], which lives in `foyer-patch`.

oneOf.description: Chunker settings the build was split with.

files.description:
Every file in the build, keyed by its `/`-separated path relative to
the build root.

Media.description: An image on a game page.

position.description: Sort order among screenshots, starting at 0.

MediaUpload.description: Upload the image with `PUT upload_url`, sending the same `Content-Type`.

Page_AppealItem.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to get the next
page; it is `None` on the last page. Cursors are opaque strings.

Page_Game.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to get the next
page; it is `None` on the last page. Cursors are opaque strings.

ai_disclosure.description:
How generative AI was used, if at all. Disclosure is required by the
content guidelines.

platforms.description: Platforms with at least one ready build.

Page_QueueItem.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to get the next
page; it is `None` on the last page. Cursors are opaque strings.

items.description: A review queue entry: the submission with the game it is for.

developer_strikes.description: The developer's strikes that still count.

flagged_builds.description:
The game's builds whose malware scan found something or could not
finish, newest first. Infected builds are never served to players.

Page_ReportedGame.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to get the next
page; it is `None` on the last page. Cursors are opaque strings.

items.description: A report queue entry: a game with open reports.

developer_strikes.description: The developer's strikes that still count.

PasswordReset.description:
`POST /v1/auth/password-reset`: the token from the reset email and the
new password. Signs out every session.

PasswordResetRequest.description:
`POST /v1/auth/password-reset/request`. Always answers 204, whether or
not an account has this address.

PolicyRule.description:
A rule from the public content guidelines. Every rejection cites one, and
a change request can point at one.

QueueItem.description: A review queue entry: the submission with the game it is for.

developer_strikes.description: The developer's strikes that still count.

flagged_builds.description:
The game's builds whose malware scan found something or could not
finish, newest first. Infected builds are never served to players.

ReasonCount.description: How many open reports give one reason.

RedeemTesterKey.description:
`POST /v1/tester-keys/redeem`: which game a key unlocks, so clients can
add a key without knowing the game.

username.description: 3 to 32 characters: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

Report.description: A player's report, as staff see it.

ReportReason.description: Why a player reported a game.

ReportedGame.description: A report queue entry: a game with open reports.

developer_strikes.description: The developer's strikes that still count.

ResolvedReports.description: How many reports a staff action closed.

Role.description: What a user is allowed to do beyond managing their own content.

ScanFinding.description: One file the scanner flagged or could not scan.

detail.description:
The scanner's signature name, e.g. `Win.Trojan.Agent-123`, or why the
file was not scanned.

Strike.description:
A recorded violation against a developer. Strikes are a record for staff
to weigh; they don't trigger anything on their own.

game.description: The game it was for, if any (its slug).

notes.description: What happened. Visible to the developer.

revoked_at.description: Set when staff took it back, e.g. after an appeal.

Submission.description:
A request to list a game (or to list it again after changes), or a
delisting by staff.

decision_notes.description: Written feedback from the reviewer. Visible to the developer.

developer_notes.description: Notes from the developer to the reviewer.

SupportKind.description:
Where players can support a developer or a game. Foyer does not sell
games; pages link out to these instead.

label.description: Optional button text, e.g. "Buy me a coffee".

channels.description: Channels the key unlocks. Empty means every channel.

TesterKey.description:
A tester key as the developer sees it. The secret is shown only once,
in [`CreatedTesterKey`].

channels.description: Channels the key unlocks. Empty means every channel.

expires_at.description: The key stops working after this. `None` never expires.

label.description: The developer's note, e.g. who the key is for.

last_used_at.description: Last time a client used the key, to the day.

prefix.description: The first characters of the secret, to tell keys apart.

unavailable.description:
Entries whose game or channel is no longer public (e.g. delisted).
The installed copy keeps working, but there is nothing to update to.

updates.description: Only entries whose channel serves a different build now.

UpdateDeveloper.description:
`PATCH /v1/developers/{slug}`. Omitted fields stay unchanged. The slug
cannot be changed.

email_verified.description:
True once the user confirmed their email address (or signed in with
Discord, which has). Needed before submitting a game for review.

UserSummary.description: Public view of a user, e.g. the reviewer on a submission.

VerifyEmailRequest.description: `POST /v1/auth/verify-email`: the token from the verification email.

tags.name: downloads
tags.description: Anonymous downloads, update checks and download counts

tags.description: Player reports, developer appeals and strikes
